newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU steps up fight against sex trade.
newsitem.headline: EU steps up fight against sex trade.

text.p: The European Commission urged EU countries and the tourism industry on Wednesday to discourage "sex tourists" from going on holiday to indulge in sex with children.

The Commission proposal came out a day before European Union interior ministers were to formalise measures to fight the sex trade in children and women, thrown into the world spotlight by a Belgian child-sex and murder scandal.

The Commission said in a policy paper that at national level EU countries should put pressure on national tourism authorities to take preventive measures against child sex tourism, and vowed to keep a closer eye on how well they were complying.
"This will contribute to a better understanding of this phenomenon and to a successful fight against it," the EU executive said in a statement.
The plan to be adopted by interior ministers on Thursday drafts the EU's police agency Europol into the fight against the trade in children and women.
The EU will also set up, through the Hague-based agency, a system allowing EU countries to pool experts in fighting the trade.

In the Belgian murder case, British Police Superintendent John Bennett was drafted in along with special radar imaging equipment used to find the bodies of missing girls and unmask British serial killers Fred and Rosemary West.
The EU ministers will also agree that police officers should take part in exchange training courses across the EU.
The ministers will also discuss how EU members could penalise people for possessing pornographic material.
Countries which do not currently punish tourists who travel overseas for child sex will be encouraged to do so, EU officials said.
